subject.title: trusted-proxy auth: support fallback/default user when identity header is absent

question: Should trusted-proxy auth support an explicit fallback identity when the configured identity header is absent on a request from a trusted proxy source?
rationale: The code change is mechanically bounded, but it changes the trusted-proxy auth boundary from requiring per-request identity evidence to allowing a configured principal based on proxy-source trust.

options.title: Approve narrow fallback mode
options.body: Add a default-off single-principal fallback with config/schema/docs/audit/test coverage for source, loopback, required-header, origin, and allowlist semantics.

options.title: Keep fail-closed identity headers
options.body: Reject headerless trusted-proxy identity and document Cloudflare Zero Trust IP-whitelist/no-identity WebSocket setups as unsupported for this auth mode.

options.title: Require live Cloudflare proof first
options.body: Ask for a reproducible Cloudflare Tunnel/WebSocket proof before accepting new OpenClaw auth surface.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow fallback mode
recommendation.body: Add a default-off single-principal fallback with config/schema/docs/audit/test coverage for source, loopback, required-header, origin, and allowlist semantics.
